## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Uppādavāra* ("Origination Section", Ya 3.2.1) is a subsection of the *Yamaka*, the sixth book of the Theravāda Abhidhamma Piṭaka. Within the *Yamaka*, the process division (*pavattivāra*) analyzes the condition of beings who are reborn or passing away in various planes and states [Anderson 1999]. This analysis is systematically organized into three sections: origination (*uppādavāra*), cessation (*nirodhavāra*), and combined origination and cessation (*uppādanirodhavāra*) [Anderson 1999; Ronkin 2005]. In the *Uppādavāra*, questions concerning the arising of phenomena are examined across time periods (present, past, and future) in both positive and negative formulations, structured systematically according to person (*puggala*), place (*okāsa*), and person and place jointly [Nyanatiloka 2007; Anderson 1999]. Scholars note that this process analysis represents early Buddhist process metaphysics and constitutes an important early stage in formulating temporal moments and the sub-moments of arising and destruction (*uppādakkhaṇa*, *bhaṅgakkhaṇa*) [Ronkin 2005].

- [Nyanatiloka 2007] Nyanatiloka Mahāthera, Guide Through the Abhidhamma Piṭaka (1938, repr. 2007) — Analytical divisions of Uppādavāra by person, place, person-and-place, and past/present
